text.p: Swedish telephone equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson was the standout among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) trading on Wednesday.

The ADR group was up overall along with the rest of Wall Street. New York stocks were boosted by a falling yield on the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond that eased interest worries, analysts and traders said.
Advancers led decliners 273 to 208 in early afternoon among 806 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.36 percent and volume was 48 million shares.
Ericcson rose 2-3/8 to 33-7/8 in heavy volume after Merrill Lynch named it the focus stock of the week and raised its rating to near-term buy from accumulate.
Fellow Nordic telecom Nokia Group also was up, rising 1-5/8 to 63-3/8.
Among other European stocks, Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 1-1/8 to 181 ahead of earnings results out Thursday.
Schroder Wertheim analyst Michael Mayer also rated the major oil companies overweight in a model stock portfolio, and rated Royal Dutch, among other companies, an outperform.
Franco-Italian semiconductor company SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV rose 3-7/8 to 78-1/8 in heavy trade. The New York Stock Exchange said the company declined to comment on the stock's activity.
Japan's Nippon Telephone and Telegraph Corp rose 3-1/2 to 39 in heavy trade after British Telecommunications Plc's chief executive said he was seeking more strategic alliances in Asia.
Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd was off 3/16 to 2-9/16 as investors awaited a report on a controversial Indonesian gold discovery.
Toronto finance company Newcourt Credit Group Inc debuted on the New York Stock Exchange and was unchanged at 18-1/2.
